newsitem.title: USA: Exogen fracture system gets PMA from FDA.
newsitem.headline: Exogen fracture system gets PMA from FDA.

text.p: Exogen Inc said Wednesday that it has received a Pre-Market Approval Supplement from the Food and Drug Administration to market the SAFHS 2000, which uses ultrasound to heal fractures.
The company said it plans to submit within the next 30 days a PMA Supplement to the FDA seeking to expand current indications for SAFHS therapy.

The Sonic Accelerated Fracture Healing System 2000 is battery operated and lighter than the first generation SAFHS Model 2A. Exogen said it believes it will see increased product margins from the product because it costs less to make.
Exogen said more than 3,000 patients have completed SAFHS therapy to date, with a 92 percent fracture healing rate reported by prescribing physicians.
